differences.what: the door's segmental stone hood and key over a pair of leaves, as the windows' hoods; built as a plain K07 door in a square hole
the iron balconettes under the two north principal windows (the north one broader, on scrolled consoles); not built: the kit lays a balcony only on a bay
the stoop's cast-iron railings, scrolled panels on newels, over open steps; built with K07's solid stone cheeks
a stone belt across the front at the second floor and a thin band at the principal heads, which K01's stone front lays and the print does not show
the north flank's basement is light stone in the print, like the front's; built in the flank's common brick to grade
the north wall ends at the bay's far side in the print (sky beyond; the 1911 sheet steps the wall back 1.26 m behind the bay); built running on to the rear at full width
the bay's lights round-headed, its stone base with a round-headed basement light, and its top a bracketed cornice; built square-headed under a plain cap
the cornice's depth: a tall plain frieze with panels between paired carved brackets about 1.1 m deep; K10's cornice is shallower and its brackets smaller
the basement lights are round-headed in the print; K06's area light is square-headed
the walk passes through the stone wall in the print; K11's coping wall is unbroken

the roof: a low hipped roof with a broad centre gable and an oculus over the front, two tall stacks; the 1904 house carries the mansard storey of 1886 the photograph predates (the register; the 1911 sheet's 3 storeys), built reconstructed over the same cornice. A picture before 1886 is evidence of its date (AGENTS.md rule 11), so its roof is not copied into 1904
colour: the print is monochrome; only the front's brick reading darker than its stone and the sunlit flank is read
the south flank and the rear, which the camera does not see
the hoods' short ears at their springing, which K06's band does not carve
the round-headed pair's lights set 0.4 m apart, the kit's least between read windows, where the print shows a narrow mullion
